# Unsloth Studio Installation Summary

**Image Name & Tags:**

- 8888 (Jupyter)

- 2222 (SSH)

**Required Environment Variables:**
- `JUPYTER_PASSWORD` (set your password)

**Volume Mounts:**
- `-v $(pwd)/work:/workspace/work` (workspace directory)

**GPU Requirements:**
- `--gpus all` flag required
- NVIDIA GPU support (specific compute capability/VRAM not documented)

**Launch Command:**
```bash
docker run -d -e JUPYTER_PASSWORD="mypassword" \
  -p 8888:8888 -p 8000:8000 -p 2222:22 \
  -v $(pwd)/work:/workspace/work \
  --gpus all \
  unsloth/unsloth
```

**Access:** `http://localhost:8000` or `http://external_ip_address:8000/`

## Non-Docker Installation Options

# Implementation Plan — `21-unsloth-studio` bundle

## Step 1: Create `21-unsloth-studio/fleet.yaml`

Model on `/06-milvus/attu/fleet.yaml`: a 3–4 line bundle-specific header, then `defaultNamespace: ai`, then the standard 8-line `takeOwnership` comment copied verbatim, then `helm: {takeOwnership: true}`.

Header content (bundle-specific part):

```yaml
# Fleet bundle — Unsloth Studio, web GUI for LLM fine-tuning (raw manifest).
# GPU-pinned to the V100 by UUID via runtimeClassName: nvidia (NOT the device
# plugin); Deployment declared at replicas: 0 — ollama holds the same V100.
# Prerequisites before enabling this path: the unsloth-jupyter Secret must
# exist in ai (see README.md), and cert-manager + letsencrypt-dns must be live
# (Ingress at unsloth.ash4d.com).
defaultNamespace: ai

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — ...
# [copy the remaining takeOwnership comment verbatim from 06-milvus/attu/fleet.yaml]
helm:
  takeOwnership: true
```

Note: unlike every other bundle, this one has no pre-existing live objects, so `takeOwnership` is a no-op on first sync — keep it anyway for convention consistency (it protects a future re-adopt after manual `kubectl apply`).

## Step 2: Create `21-unsloth-studio/unsloth-studio.yaml` — single file, four objects

Confirmed structure: one manifest with Deployment + PVC + Service + Ingress, following `comfyui.yaml` (GPU Deployment + PVC) and `attu.yaml` (ClusterIP Service + Traefik Ingress) exactly.

### Deployment — key fields

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: unsloth-studio, namespace: ai, labels: {app: unsloth-studio}}
spec:
  # SCALED TO ZERO on purpose — same V100 contention comment block as
  # comfyui.yaml lines 9-14, adapted: "bump it here, not with kubectl scale,
  # or the next reconcile puts it back."
  replicas: 0
  strategy:
    type: Recreate          # RWO PVC + exclusive GPU — no rolling update
  template:
    spec:
      runtimeClassName: nvidia
      containers:
      - name: unsloth-studio
        # Pinned tag == today's `latest` digest (verified 2026-07-30,
        # sha256:f21629b9ae4e...). The repo publishes versioned tags weekly;
        # bump deliberately, never track latest — this is a 13 GB pull.
        image: unsloth/unsloth:2026.5.9-pt2.10.0-vllm-0.16.0-cu12.8-studio-release-v0.1.43-beta-2026-MAY-31
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        env:
        # GPU pin: Tesla V100 32GB, NOT GPU 0 (GTX 1070). Same UUID and same
        # rationale comment as comfyui.yaml lines 30-36.
        - name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
          value: GPU-a69c6398-0353-3234-9f35-af0e02865f33
        - name: NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES
          value: compute,utility
        - name: JUPYTER_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef: {name: unsloth-jupyter, key: JUPYTER_PASSWORD}
        # Keep HF model/tokenizer cache on the PVC alongside /workspace/work
        # so a pod restart does not re-download base models.
        - name: HF_HOME
          value: /workspace/work/.hf-home
        ports:
        - {containerPort: 8000, name: studio}
        - {containerPort: 8888, name: jupyter}
        resources:            # see Step 6 rationale; NO nvidia.com/gpu entry
          requests: {cpu: "2", memory: 8Gi}
          limits: {cpu: "6", memory: 28Gi}
        volumeMounts:
        - {mountPath: /workspace/work, name: data, subPath: work}
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: unsloth-data}
```

Design notes to carry as comments in the file:
- **No `nvidia.com/gpu` request** — comment mirroring `04-ollama/values.yaml:66-75`: the device plugin would inject its own `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and could hand out GPU 0.
- **Single mount + `HF_HOME` redirect** rather than a second subPath at `/root/.cache/huggingface`: the image's convention is `/workspace/work`; steering the HF cache under that mount keeps one PVC/one mount and guarantees everything that must survive a restart (datasets, checkpoints, LoRA adapters, base-model cache) lives on Longhorn. This is the comfyui lesson ("BOTH must be PVC-backed or installs die with the pod") solved with one mount instead of two.
- **V100 caveat comment**: SM 7.0 — fp16 only, no bf16, no flash-attention-2. The image is built for cu12.8/vLLM 0.16; V100 (compute 7.0) is within support, but any Studio run must select fp16, not bf16.
- No SSH_KEY / USER_PASSWORD env — SSH (22) deliberately unexposed.

### PVC

```yaml
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: unsloth-data, namespace: ai}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 60Gi}}
  storageClassName: longhorn   # explicit — cluster default is local-path
```

**Sizing rationale (goes in README):** Longhorn is at ~412Gi of ~500Gi allocated. 60Gi fits a 7B fp16 base model (~15GB HF cache), datasets, and several LoRA checkpoint sets, while keeping nominal allocation at ~472Gi. Longhorn supports online PVC expansion, so start small and grow deliberately rather than repeating the 150Gi comfyui claim. Full-model (non-LoRA) fine-tuning checkpoints would blow this budget — that workload should not happen on this pool anyway.

### Service + Ingress

Copy `attu.yaml` verbatim in shape:
- Service `unsloth-studio`, `type: ClusterIP` (with the "does not need to burn a MetalLB IP" comment), port 8000 → targetPort 8000. Studio only — **do not** add 8888 to the Service.
- Ingress `unsloth-studio`, `ingressClassName: traefik`, host `unsloth.ash4d.com`, annotation `cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-dns`, TLS secret `unsloth-ash4d-tls`.

**Jupyter decision: do not expose 8888 via ingress.** Rationale (document in README): Jupyter gives arbitrary code execution in a GPU pod; the Studio UI is the purpose of this bundle; and the pod is normally at replicas 0 anyway. README documents `kubectl -n ai port-forward deploy/unsloth-studio 8888:8888` for occasional notebook use. If it later earns an ingress, it is a second host (`unsloth-jupyter.ash4d.com`) with its own TLS secret — not a path under the Studio host, since Jupyter's base-URL handling under a path prefix is fragile. SSH 22: skipped entirely.

## Step 3: Secret handling (manual, pre-Fleet)

Follow the hermes pattern exactly (`10-hermes/README.md` lines 3–11 and the prerequisite blockquote):

```bash
kubectl -n ai create secret generic unsloth-jupyter \
  --from-literal=JUPYTER_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -base64 24)"
```

## Step 4: Create `21-unsloth-studio/README.md`

Outline, modeled on `07-comfyui/README.md` and `10-hermes/README.md`:

1. **Install commands block** at top: the `kubectl create secret` command, then `kubectl apply -f unsloth-studio.yaml` (for hand-testing before Fleet), then the GitRepo patch (below).

3. **GPU section**: the replicas-0/V100-contention paragraph, copied in spirit from comfyui's README ("Scale to 1 by editing the yaml, not `kubectl scale`"), plus scale-up procedure vs Ollama (Step 8 below).
4. **V100 constraints**: SM 7.0 → fp16 only, no bf16, no flash-attention-2; Studio runs must select fp16. Image is CUDA 12.8 — host driver must satisfy CUDA 12.x minor-version compat (`nvidia-smi` on sdf1 shows the driver's max CUDA; verify ≥ 12.8 or rely on forward compat).
5. **Storage rationale**: 60Gi/Longhorn-pressure paragraph, `HF_HOME` redirect explanation, expansion note.
6. **Resource limits rationale** (Step 6).
7. **DNS note**: `unsloth.ash4d.com` must resolve (add the record wherever the other `*.ash4d.com` hosts live) before cert-manager's DNS-01 order and browser access work.

## Step 5: GitRepo wiring — patch `lab-ai`, no new file

Per `/14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md`: `lab-ai` deliberately has no `.yaml` — do not create one. Two repo edits + one cluster command:

1. Update the staged-commands block in `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md` (the `spec.paths` patch example around lines 102–109 and the `lab-ai` status row) to include `21-unsloth-studio` as the next single-entry append.
2. The actual widen (run only after the Secret exists and the commit is pushed):

```bash
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-ai --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"paths":[ <current live list...>, "21-unsloth-studio" ]}}'
```

Append exactly one entry per the one-at-a-time rule. **Read the current live `spec.paths` first** (`kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo lab-ai -o jsonpath='{.spec.paths}'`) — the README's list may lag what was patched since (04-ollama etc. were pending as of 2026-07-30). Since this is a fresh install (no adoption), risk is low; the removal-uninstalls warning still applies afterward.

## Step 6: Resources rationale (64GB shared host)

- Requests `cpu: 2 / memory: 8Gi`: enough for dataloader/tokenizer work; low enough that a replicas-0→1 flip schedules even with ollama, milvus, emby, open-webui, etc. resident.
- Limits `cpu: 6 / memory: 28Gi`: fine-tuning host-RAM use is dominated by dataset prep and optimizer state paging; 28Gi caps a runaway before it OOMs the single node that runs everything (k3s control plane included). 3700X has 16 threads — cap at 6 CPUs so a tokenization burst can't starve the node.
- No GPU resource entries (see discrepancy note above).

## Step 7: Commit

Single commit adding the three files in `21-unsloth-studio/` plus the `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md` edit. (Repo root `README.md` — check whether it carries a bundle index; the top-level dir listing suggests numbered dirs are self-documenting, but scan it for a table that needs a `21` row.)

## Step 8: Verification

1. **Bundle deployed**: the custom-columns check from `gitrepos/README.md` — `READY: true`, `NONMODIFIED: true` for the new `lab-ai-21-unsloth-studio` bundledeployment; `helm -n ai list` shows one new release at revision 1.
2. **Objects present, pod absent**: `kubectl -n ai get deploy,pvc,svc,ingress -l app=unsloth-studio` → Deployment 0/0, PVC `Bound` on longhorn, Service ClusterIP, Ingress with address.
3. **Cert issued**: `kubectl -n ai get certificate unsloth-ash4d-tls` → Ready (cert-manager issues even with the Deployment at 0; Traefik will 502 until scale-up, which is fine).
4. **Scale-up against Ollama** (README procedure): free the V100 first — either scale `ollama` to 0 (`kubectl -n ai scale sts/deploy ollama --replicas=0`, remembering Fleet will fight this once `04-ollama` is Fleet-owned, so prefer the API unload: `curl http://<ollama>/api/generate -d '{"model":"<name>","keep_alive":0}'`) and confirm with host `nvidia-smi` that the V100 shows ~0 MiB. Then edit `replicas: 1` in `unsloth-studio.yaml`, commit, push, wait for Fleet's 60s poll. Reverse to scale down.
5. **First-run smoke test**:
   - Pod pulls ~13GB image (first start is slow — `kubectl -n ai get events` / `describe pod` to watch the pull).
   - `kubectl -n ai exec deploy/unsloth-studio -- nvidia-smi` → exactly one GPU, `Tesla V100`, matching UUID; the GTX 1070 must not appear.

   - Restart the pod and confirm no model re-download (HF cache persistence proof).

Sequencing summary: files + commit → Secret in `ai` → DNS record → GitRepo patch → verify at replicas 0 → scale-up smoke test → scale back to 0.

- /Users/rashford/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Developer/lab-fleet/21-unsloth-studio/unsloth-studio.yaml (new — Deployment/PVC/Service/Ingress)

# 21 — Unsloth Studio

Web GUI for LLM fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA and full fine-tuning) on the V100,
from the official `unsloth/unsloth` image — Studio UI on 8000 at
[unsloth.ash4d.com](https://unsloth.ash4d.com), Jupyter Lab on 8888 at
[jupyter.ash4d.com](https://jupyter.ash4d.com). SSH (port 22 in the image) is
deliberately not exposed.

## Install

The Secret must exist **before** the Fleet path is enabled or the pod sticks
in `CreateContainerConfigError`:

```bash
kubectl -n ai create secret generic unsloth-jupyter \
  --from-literal=JUPYTER_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -base64 24)"
```

Hand-test without Fleet (optional):

```bash
kubectl apply -f unsloth-studio.yaml
```

Enable via Fleet by appending this path to the live `lab-ai` GitRepo — read the
current list first and append exactly one entry (see
`14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md`):

```bash
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo lab-ai -o jsonpath='{.spec.paths}'
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-ai --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"paths":[ <current live list...>, "21-unsloth-studio" ]}}'
```

Unlike the other `lab-ai` paths this is a **fresh install, not an adoption** —
Fleet deploys it as soon as the path lands, so the Secret and DNS
(`unsloth.ash4d.com`, `jupyter.ash4d.com` → Traefik) must already be in place.

## Image / version pinning

`unsloth/unsloth` publishes versioned tags; the pinned
`2026.5.9-pt2.10.0-vllm-0.16.0-cu12.8-studio-release-v0.1.43-beta-2026-MAY-31`
equals the `latest` digest verified 2026-07-30 (`sha256:f21629b9ae4e…`). Bump
the tag deliberately — it is a ~13 GB pull, so the first pod start on a new tag
is slow. Building a custom image (e.g. on SUSE BCI) was considered and
rejected: it would mean recreating the CUDA 12.8 / PyTorch 2.10 / Triton /
vLLM stack by hand for zero benefit.

The image is CUDA 12.8 — the host driver must satisfy CUDA 12.x compat
(`nvidia-smi` on sdf1 shows the driver's max supported CUDA version).

## GPU: replicas 0, V100 by UUID

Same pattern and same reason as ComfyUI (`07-comfyui/`): GPU access is
`runtimeClassName: nvidia` plus an explicit `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` UUID —
**not** a device-plugin `nvidia.com/gpu` request, which would let the plugin
override the pin and possibly hand out the 8 GB GTX 1070. The pinned UUID is
the Tesla V100 that Ollama holds with `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`, so this
Deployment is **declared at `replicas: 0`**.

### Starting a fine-tuning session

1. Free the V100. Prefer the API unload over scaling ollama (Fleet will fight
   `kubectl scale` once `04-ollama` is Fleet-owned):

   ```bash
   curl http://192.168.7.153/api/generate -d '{"model":"<loaded-model>","keep_alive":0}'
   ```

   Confirm on the host that the V100 shows ~0 MiB used: `nvidia-smi`.
2. Edit `replicas: 1` in `unsloth-studio.yaml`, commit, push; Fleet's 60s poll
   picks it up. (Before Fleet owns this path, `kubectl -n ai scale deploy
   unsloth-studio --replicas=1` works too.)
3. When done, reverse: set `replicas: 0`, then load the ollama model again
   (any request to ollama reloads it).

### V100 constraints

SM 7.0 (Volta): **fp16 only — no bf16, no flash-attention-2.** Pick fp16 in
Studio's training options; bf16 runs will fail or silently fall back. 4-bit
QLoRA and fp16 LoRA both work; FP8 does not.

## Storage

One 100Gi Longhorn PVC (`unsloth-data`), single mount at `/workspace/work`
(the image's working-directory convention). `HF_HOME` is redirected to
`/workspace/work/.hf-home` so the base-model cache, datasets, and checkpoints
all live on the one PVC and survive pod restarts — the ComfyUI lesson ("both
mounts must be PVC-backed or installs die with the pod") solved with a single
mount.

100Gi fits a couple of 13B-class fp16 base models plus datasets and LoRA
checkpoints. The Longhorn pool was at ~412Gi of ~500Gi allocated before this
claim; expand online (Longhorn supports it) rather than over-claiming. Do not
run full-model checkpoint-heavy fine-tunes against this pool.

## Resources

Requests `2 CPU / 8Gi`, limits `6 CPU / 28Gi`. The node is a single 16-thread
3700X with 64 GB running everything including the k3s control plane: the low
request keeps a `replicas: 0→1` flip schedulable with ollama, milvus, emby et
al. resident; the limits cap a runaway tokenization/dataset-prep burst before
it starves the node. No GPU resource entries (see above).

## Security

Jupyter is arbitrary code execution in a GPU pod behind a single password —
the `unsloth-jupyter` Secret. Never leave the image default (`unsloth`); the
create command above generates a random one. Retrieve it with:

```bash
kubectl -n ai get secret unsloth-jupyter -o jsonpath='{.data.JUPYTER_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d
```

TLS on both hosts via cert-manager (`letsencrypt-dns` DNS-01), certs issue
even while the Deployment sits at 0 (Traefik 502s until scale-up — expected).
